summary: Suspend external-grant authentication when replicated grants assign opposite profiles to one principal

replay.detail: Existing append-only grant, policy and revocation claims are preserved without rewriting history. Additive external-grant authority projection version 1 is populated by a resumable background backfill. Active opposite-profile grants conflict regardless of replication arrival order; revoked and expired grants do not contribute to the conflict.

schema.detail: Adds external-grant authority projection version 1 as additive store state; older builds can still open an upgraded store. The durable assistant_grant_local_appends(claim_id PRIMARY KEY) table records only new local insert_claim appends, never inferred historical or replicated provenance. Projection version remains 1 (unreleased). Adds typed client error assistant-grant-authority-not-ready with retryable=true (HTTP 503) while assistant authorization fails closed during background backfill. Also adds grant-profile-conflict (HTTP 409). Bearer authentication and pairing disclose only the conflict code and fixed message principal has active grants of opposite profiles; revoke one to clear the conflict, without witness details. Only daemon-configured-owner inspection with ?witness=1 exposes conflict and cleared_conflicts witnesses with typed assistant/service profiles and revoked/expired causes. Default grant responses retain their previous shape for old strict clients.

rules.detail: Assistant authorization fails closed until the local authority projection backfill is ready. After initial backfill, dirty or pending authentication, including a pending revoke, fences only its grant subject; unrelated established credentials remain usable. Fresh signatures from keys outside the writer's admitted window do not reset authentication cursors or queue projection work. Membership invalidation reuses the inherited fleet generation for changes to projected writer/key/start/end windows, including delayed bootstrap evidence; there is no separate projection revision or copied trigger set. Folding and comparison run on readers outside receipt transactions; an unchanged window snapshot advances only an in-memory observation, without writer admission or cursor resets. Pure additions retry unauthenticated rows only. Each authenticated remote row records its complete proof identity: writer, sequence, envelope hash, record position and member key; local-append provenance remains a separate durable fact. Signature DELETE/UPDATE, record invalidation/deletion and envelope invalidation/deletion enqueue exact proof dependencies in the mutating transaction, independently of membership changes. Indexed maintenance authenticates one dependent claim per unit. Retractions revisit only recorded key/sequence dependencies that lost coverage and fence only those subjects; restored coverage exempts covered dependencies immediately and queued ranges are trimmed or cancelled within the budget. Legitimate authenticated-member key removal still costs O(rows authenticated by that key) across bounded transactions, with affected subjects fenced until rechecked. Per-base authority deletion and indexed latest-transition recomputation share the 64-unit budget with changed windows and authentication. The resulting projection equals a fresh backfill of current evidence, including removal of revoked authority; unauthenticated transitions still fence bearer use. Inherited reader-side signature aggregation remains a pre-existing cost tracked by #6124. Writer-time pending-subject checks retain generic authorization denials; clean-grant inspection omits optional explanations for other pending subjects while preserving established authenticated conflict witnesses. If a principal has active grants in both assistant and service profiles, all of that principal's external grants are suspended, not just the losing or newest profile. Multiple same-profile grants remain allowed. Authentication resumes after replicated append-only revocations or expiry remove the opposite-profile conflict from the local view. The configured owner can revoke existing service-profile history through trusted-local Unix without changing its immutable profile; service issuance, policy updates and requests remain disabled. Owner inspection reports active witnesses and cleared_conflicts witnesses with revoked or expired causes from the authority projection and retained evidence.

compatibility.detail: Conflict admission counts only well-formed owner grants. New local appends require durable local-append provenance; unmarked historical claims, including claims naming this local origin, require a verified member envelope signature and matching admitted membership window. Unsigned or unsealed Legacy history is not grandfathered into authority. Grants issued before upgrade without a verifiable member signature stay unusable and must be reissued by the configured owner. Logical backup restore assigns a new writer and does not carry local-append markers; unsigned pre-restore grants fail closed and require the same configured-owner reissue procedure. Policies and revocations count only from the grant's own origin and owner with consistent immutable identity. A newer unauthenticated transition cannot hide an older authenticated renewal. Invalid overlays are ignored, retaining the last valid policy. Projection version 1 is additive and raw append-only evidence remains authoritative and intact. Tokens remain issuer-local. Rollback to an older build is supported, but older members do not enforce these provenance checks, the new projection readiness gate or conflict suspension, so upgrade all serving members before relying on them.

downtime.detail: No offline migration window is planned: startup backfill has an approximately two-second budget, then continues in bounded background slices. A synthetic 3.73 GB store with one million claims and 1% grant-kind rows measured a 1.892-second startup slice and 1.919-second total backfill, with 54,940 KiB process peak RSS; linear same-mix throughput extrapolation to 50 GB is 25.750 seconds, not a production or cold-cache guarantee. The startup slice excludes Store::open and does not predict total daemon startup time. Assistant authorization is temporarily unavailable with retryable assistant-grant-authority-not-ready until the local projection is ready; this is an authorization interruption, not a requirement to stop the daemon for the entire backfill. Affected people also cannot authenticate with any external grant while a profile conflict remains visible; a partition can extend that interruption until revocations replicate.

manual.detail: Allow the resumable background backfill to finish before retrying assistant authorization after assistant-grant-authority-not-ready. Run fractal doctor: the claim-store section lists each unauthenticated unmarked local grant claim ID with reason grant predates local-append provenance; re-issue. Remote unmarked grants are separately reported as lacking verified provenance with issuance age unknown, not definitively pre-upgrade. The same private provenance check lists subject-maintenance causes: dirty claims awaiting projection, signature authentication cursors, unauthenticated grant/policy/revocation evidence, and writer membership revalidation queued beyond its durable cursor. During a transient subject fence, bearer clients intentionally receive generic credential rejection rather than the maintenance cause, avoiding an authentication oracle. Detailed subjects, causes, grant IDs, origin and actor remain trusted-local doctor diagnostics and are excluded from paired-client operations collection and detail reads, including read.projections clients. For unusable pre-upgrade or unsigned pre-restore grants, the configured owner reissues through trusted-local Unix with fractal devices --as person/OWNER pair --assistant assistant/mcp --scope read.assistant.summary --disclose-to-openai --consent-evidence '<recorded owner consent reference>' (select the original principal and explicitly approved scopes), then completes the new challenge with fractal devices complete MEMBER_URL PAIRING_ID --assistant --profile /absolute/path/to/new-profile.json and replaces the protected adapter credential. There is no in-place reissue command or SQL provenance repair. Service issuance remains disabled. For a conflicted principal, choose the intended profile and append revocations for every active grant in the opposite profile. Let those revocations replicate to each serving issuer. Do not delete raw claims, clear append-only evidence, or replace tokens to resolve a conflict or restart the backfill.

recovery.detail: Restarting resumes the background backfill idempotently from retained progress; no raw claim deletion or manual data rewrite is required. Rollback to an older build is supported because projection version 1 is additive and preserves raw evidence, but the older build does not provide the new authorization guarantees. After revocations replicate, remaining otherwise-valid grants in the intended profile can authenticate again without reissuance. Expiry of every remaining active opposite-profile grant also clears the conflict; expired and revoked grants remain unusable. If a ready issuer still reports a conflict after revocation, restore replication so it receives the revocations; restarting or changing claim arrival order does not resolve the conflict.
